transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Thanks for seeing me. Well, what pushed me to make this appointment is... I mean, I'm an accountant, right? So I do a lot of audits, and I also help out with these mentorship events for junior staff. And lately, I keep starting follow-up items after these audits or events, and I have every intention of finishing them. I really do. But then I'll find out days later that the final email, or a review note, or some important form never actually got done. It's so frustrating. 

Speaking of the mentorship events, we just had one last week at this hotel downtown, and the catering was just awful. I mean, they served these tiny, dry sandwiches, and they ran out of coffee halfway through the morning. Can you imagine accountants without coffee? It was a disaster. I actually ended up running across the street to a Starbucks just to get something decent, and I ran into my old neighbor, Sarah, while I was there. She just got a new puppy, a golden retriever, and she was showing me all these pictures on her phone. They were so cute, but anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the follow-up items. Yeah, I just keep leaving things half-finished, and it's starting to really affect my work.
When you're working on these follow-up items, do you find it hard to concentrate on them, or do you start them but then your mind just wanders to other things?

Well, it's a bit of both, honestly. Like, I can start out totally fine. If I have a really long client meeting, or... oh, we just had this training for a new AI tool we're supposed to be using for data extraction. I can start off fully engaged, taking notes, the whole nine yards. But after a while, my mind just slips off. I'll realize I've completely missed the last few minutes of what someone was saying, even though I'm sitting right there, staring straight at the screen. 

Which, by the way, those AI tools are getting so crazy. My nephew was telling me he uses one to write his college essays, which I told him is basically cheating, but he swears everyone does it. He's at State, studying... gosh, what is it? Environmental science, I think. He wants to work in forestry. He’s always loved trees, even when he was little. We used to go camping up near the lake... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, concentrating. Yeah, I just drift off, even when I'm looking right at whatever I'm supposed to be doing.
Over the past few weeks, how has your overall mood been? Have you been feeling down, sad, or just kind of empty most of the time?

No, I wouldn't say that. I haven't really been feeling sad or empty. I mean, I get frustrated with myself about the work stuff, sure, but my overall mood is fine. 

Actually, my coworker Brenda was just saying she felt kind of empty the other day, but I think it's because her youngest just went off to college. Empty nest syndrome, you know? She has twins, actually. Can you imagine having two kids move out and go to college at the exact same time? The tuition alone must be an absolute nightmare. As an accountant, I can't even look at those numbers without wincing. I was looking at average tuition rates the other day just out of curiosity, and they have completely skyrocketed since I got my degree. Back then, I just went to a state school and worked part-time at this little diner to pay for it... they made the absolute best cherry pie. I haven't had a good slice of cherry pie in years. My grandmother used to bake them from scratch every Thanksgiving, with the little lattice crust on top and everything. 

Anyway... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, my mood. Yeah, no, I haven't been feeling down or anything like that.
When you're sitting at your desk trying to work or in meetings, do you find yourself fidgeting, moving around a lot, or feeling restless—like you have trouble staying still?

Oh, definitely. Meetings are probably the worst for that. I'm always tapping my foot under the table, or clicking my pen without even realizing I'm doing it. I shift around in my chair so much that my colleague—Brenda, the one I was just telling you about with the twins—she actually joked the other day that she can hear my leg going under the desk. 

Which is funny she phrased it like that, because it reminds me of a jackrabbit. Actually, speaking of jackrabbits, my husband and I went to Arizona last spring. Sedona, specifically. Have you ever been? The red rocks are just absolutely stunning. Anyway, we were on this hiking trail, the Bell Rock pathway I think it was called, and we saw this massive jackrabbit. Its ears were huge! It just sat there staring at us for the longest time. We took so many pictures, but the lighting was weird because it was right around golden hour. Everyone says golden hour is the best time for photography, but I can never get my phone camera to focus right when the sun is low like that. I really think I need to upgrade to the new iPhone. The camera on the new one is supposed to be incredible, like professional grade. My niece has it, and she takes these amazing portraits of her cats... they look like they belong in a magazine. 

Wait, what was I... oh, right, fidgeting! Sorry about that. But yes, the tapping and the shifting around, I just have a really hard time staying still in my chair.
Have you had these difficulties with concentration, fidgeting, and leaving tasks incomplete for most of your life, or did they start more recently?

Well, it's definitely not a new thing. I've been like this for as long as I can remember. Even back in elementary school, my report cards always said the same thing. The teachers would write that I was bright, but I constantly lost my assignments, rushed through my work and missed small details, and talked out of turn. They were always telling me I needed reminders to finish what I started. 

Actually, my mother still jokes about it. She says I could completely ace a test, but then I'd completely forget to turn in the big project that was sitting right there in my backpack. Backpacks were so different back then, weren't they? I had this bright neon pink one from Lisa Frank. Do you remember Lisa Frank? With the rainbow dolphins and the unicorns? I was obsessed with that stuff. I had the folders, the pencils, the trapper keeper... oh my gosh, trapper keepers! Whatever happened to those? They were so satisfying to snap shut. My daughter uses these plain, boring binders now for middle school. Everything is so minimalist these days. I was looking at her school supply list in August, and it was just... black binder, blue pens, white paper. Where's the fun in that? When I was her age, we used those gel pens that smelled like fruit. The grape one was my favorite. I used to write all my notes to my best friend Sarah in that grape pen. Sarah actually just moved to Portland... or was it Seattle? Somewhere in the Pacific Northwest. It rains a lot there. I don't think I could handle all that rain. I need the sun, you know? 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, if this is new. No, it's been my whole life. The report cards, the lost projects, the fidgeting... it's just always been there.

When you were a kid, besides the fidgeting and losing things, did teachers or your parents notice you doing things impulsively—like interrupting people, blurting things out, or having trouble waiting your turn?

Yeah, definitely. I still do it now, actually. I catch myself jumping into conversations before people finish, especially with the junior auditors at work. The answer or the idea just feels so urgent in my head, and I just blurt it out before I can even stop myself. It's like I already know where their sentence is going, so I just want to get to the point. 

Which reminds me, one of the junior auditors, Kevin, he takes forever to get to the point. He's a really sweet kid, just graduated from Ohio State. My husband's family is from Ohio, actually. Cincinnati. They make that chili there, the one they put over spaghetti? Skyline Chili, I think it's called. My mother-in-law makes it every time we visit, and she always piles on this massive mountain of shredded cheddar cheese. It's honestly a little overwhelming. I'm somewhat lactose intolerant anyway, so I really shouldn't be eating all that cheese. I tried those dairy-free cheeses once, but they don't melt right. They just get kind of... sweaty? It's really unappetizing. I was watching this cooking show the other night, one of those baking championships, and they had to make a vegan cake. The judges were so critical of the frosting texture. I don't know how those bakers handle the pressure with the clock ticking down like that. I would be a nervous wreck. 

Anyway... um, what were we talking about? Oh, right, blurting things out. Yeah, I've always had trouble waiting my turn to speak.

Beyond just the frustration with work tasks, has this difficulty with attention and fidgeting actually caused real problems in your relationships, your job performance, or other areas of your life—like have you gotten in trouble at work, or has it affected your relationships with family or friends?

Well, yes, it's... it's definitely causing real issues now. At work, it's gotten pretty bad. I've made mistakes, and I leave follow-ups unfinished, and it actually affected a client review recently. It's so frustrating because I know the material, but I just miss things. I'm really worried people are starting to question whether I can even handle this promotion I'm up for. 

Which is so stressful because we really need the extra income if we're going to redo the kitchen. We've been talking about remodeling for years. The cabinets are this awful honey oak color from the nineties, and the hinges keep sticking. My husband tried WD-40, but it just smells like a garage now. Have you noticed how strong that smell is? It lingers forever. We were looking at those new smart refrigerators, the ones with the screens on the door where you can see inside without opening it. But they're so expensive! I don't know if we really need a fridge that connects to the Wi-Fi. What if it gets hacked? I read an article about people's smart home devices getting hacked, like their thermostats and baby monitors. It's terrifying to think about someone controlling your house from the internet. We don't even have a smart thermostat, just the old dial kind, but it works fine. 

But anyway, yeah, the problems... it's not just work, it's at home too. My husband has actually had to take over paying the bills and handling commitments I agreed to. He says he just can't count on me to complete them reliably anymore. It makes me feel terrible, but I just... I forget, or I put it off and then it's too late.
